proofs.proof_tex:
We give complete panel experiments.  It suffices to work conditionally on a fixed value of \(E_0\), because all displayed laws below are regular conditional laws and the unconditional law is obtained by integrating them against any event-state law supported on the declared positive-probability region.  Choose an interior point \(x_\circ\) whose distance from the boundary exceeds \(\delta_0\).  Let the \(X_{st}\) be independent uniform vectors on \([0,1]^d\), independently over \(s,t\).  Thus their conditional density is one, their conditional beta-mixing coefficients are zero, and \(c_X\le1\le C_X\).  Set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).

We first describe a common causal completion.  Choose regression values in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,B)\).  Conditional on the complete design \(\mathscr X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), generate the \(Q_{sti}\) independently over \((s,i)\), with bounded two-point laws having mean \(m_s(X_{st})\) and conditional variance at least \(B^{-1}\).  The perturbation constants below are chosen small enough that the probabilities of both support points stay uniformly away from zero.  This is possible for every nonempty instance of the maintained bounded-support, positive-variance, and nonconstant-modulus class: those three requirements give strict interior slack.  Then
\[
\varepsilon_{sti}=Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st}),\qquad
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\]
Generate the event observations independently over \((s,i)\), independently of \(\mathscr X\), with the means specified below.  Consequently
\[
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0].
\]
For unobserved event counterfactuals choose \(B_{si}(0)\) with conditional mean \(m_s(z_{0s})\), put \(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and set \(Q_{sti}(a)=Q_{sti}\).  These assignments verify consistency, historical consistency, no spillovers, limited anticipation, and event transport.  They also verify conditional cross-unit independence and within-site replication.  Hence the two additional full-design restrictions hold by construction, rather than as consequences of contemporaneous regression or cross-unit independence.

Take a bounded Holder background \(m^\circ=(m_s^\circ)_{s\le S}\), with range in the same compact interior interval, whose weighted surface has the required two-sided modulus.  Such a background can be written explicitly: for \(\lambda>1\), use a sufficiently small nonzero affine coordinate; for \(0<\lambda\le1\), use a sufficiently small one-sided \(\lambda\)-cusp.  Scaling the nonzero coefficient inside the maintained interval \([c_{\mathrm{mod}},C_{\mathrm{mod}}]\) verifies
\[
c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa
\le\omega_P(\delta;x_\circ)
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa,\qquad
0<\delta\le\delta_0.
\]
All perturbations below are multiplied by a fixed sufficiently small constant, so the Holder radius, range, variance, and both modulus inequalities remain valid.

For the treated channel, keep the design, donor law, historical law, and untreated event counterfactuals fixed.  Let the event observations be bounded Bernoulli-type variables whose two conditional means differ by \(2v_s\), where
\[
v_s=c_1\frac{\pi_s}{n_sR_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}},
\qquad
\sum_{s=1}^{S}n_sv_s^2=c_1^2,
\qquad
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sv_s=c_1R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}.
\]
Because \(\min_s n_s\to\infty\) and \(S\) is fixed, all \(v_s\) are eventually inside the fixed probability slack.  The elementary inequality
\[
p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}\le C(p-q)^2,
\qquad p,q\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon],
\]
follows by two applications of the mean-value theorem.  Therefore the joint event-sample divergence is at most
\[
C\sum_sn_sv_s^2=Cc_1^2.
\]
The causal targets differ by \(2\sum_s\pi_sv_s\), whose square is \(4c_1^2R_{\mathrm{tr}}\).

For the smoothing channel, let \(\psi\) be a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function supported on the unit ball with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Put
\[
h_s^\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)},\qquad
g_s(x)=c_2(h_s^\circ)^\lambda
\psi\!\left(\frac{x-x_\circ}{h_s^\circ}\right),
\]
and use \(m_s^\circ\) and \(m_s^\circ+g_s\) as the two regressions.  Their event treated laws are identical, while the unobserved \(B_{si}(0)\) means are adjusted to preserve event transport.  Conditional on the design, the same Bernoulli divergence bound gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{KL}(P_{0,\mathrm{sm}},P_{1,\mathrm{sm}})
&\le C\sum_s n_sT\int_{[0,1]^d}g_s(x)^2\,dx\\
&\le Cc_2^2\sum_s n_sT(h_s^\circ)^{2\lambda+d}
=Cc_2^2S.
\end{aligned}
\]
At \(x_\circ\), the target separation is \(\sum_s\pi_sc_2(h_s^\circ)^\lambda\), and nonnegativity gives
\[
\left(\sum_s\pi_sc_2(h_s^\circ)^\lambda\right)^2
\ge c_2^2\sum_s\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=c_2^2R_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\]

For the spacing channel, take a common bandwidth \(h_T=c_3T^{-1/d}\) and perturb every cohort regression by
\[
g_{s,T}(x)=c_4h_T^\lambda
\psi\!\left(\frac{x-x_\circ}{h_T}\right).
\]
Let \(\mathcal A_T\) be the event that none of the \(ST\) design points enters the support of any bump.  Since \(S\) is fixed and the support volume is \(v_\psi h_T^d\),
\[
P(\mathcal A_T)=(1-v_\psi h_T^d)^{ST}
\longrightarrow\exp(-Sv_\psi c_3^d)>0.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\) the complete observed laws under the two regressions coincide; event treated outcomes and donors were kept common, while only unobserved event counterfactuals were changed.  Thus
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,\mathrm{sp}},dP_{1,\mathrm{sp}}\}
\ge P(\mathcal A_T)\ge c>0
\]
eventually.  The target separation equals \(c_4h_T^\lambda\), so its square is \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}=cR_{\mathrm{sp}}\).  We make no Kullback--Leibler assertion: conditional on a bump being hit, arbitrarily many within-site replicates can make the two laws nearly singular.

For the donor channel, keep the historical and observed event laws fixed.  Choose a smooth location density \(g\) on \(\mathbb R^{Sd}\) with mean zero, covariance \(\Sigma\) satisfying the declared ellipticity bounds, standardized fourth moment at most \(B\), and finite translation information.  Such a density can be chosen with compactly tapered tails and then linearly standardized within the fixed moment slack.  If \(u_N\) is a covariance-standardized direction with
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2=c_5N^{-1/2},
\]
use donor densities \(g(z-z_\circ)\) and \(g(z-z_\circ-u_N)\).  Taylor's formula for \(\log g\), followed by integration, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}\{g(\,\cdot-z_\circ),g(\,\cdot-z_\circ-u_N)\}
\le C_g\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2,
\]
and hence the \(N\)-sample divergence is at most \(C_gc_5^2\).  Choose the direction along the affine coordinate when \(\lambda>1\) and along the active side of the cusp when \(\lambda\le1\).  The two target values then satisfy
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{don}}}(z_\circ+u_N)
-\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{don}}}(z_\circ)|
\ge c\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^\kappa
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\]
Both centers remain interior for all large \(N\).  This proves the donor separation \(cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For the three bounded-divergence pairs, the elementary likelihood-ratio argument
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=\mathbb E_{P_0}[\min\{1,dP_1/dP_0\}]
\ge \tfrac12\exp\{-2\operatorname{KL}(P_0,P_1)\}
\]
after restricting to \(\{dP_1/dP_0\ge e^{-2\operatorname{KL}}\}\) gives a positive constant; decreasing \(c_1,c_2,c_5\) makes this affinity as close to one as required for a fixed \(\alpha<1/2\).  The spacing affinity was proved directly.  Every construction uses an observed joint panel and unobserved potential outcomes on the same probability space, and every law satisfies the two full-design restrictions.  Thus all four pairs lie in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), completing the embedding.

By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl},
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_s\pi_s
\{\mathbb E[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
The equality conditions on \(z_0,E_0\), but \(z_0=\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]\) is \(E_0\)-measurable.  Let \(\mathscr F\) be the complete historical design, event state, and donor sample.  Exactly as in \texttt{lem:exact-full-data-interval-calibration}, decompose
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=\mathcal E_{\mathrm{evt}}-\mathcal E_{\mathrm{hist}}
-\mathcal B_L-\mathcal B_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Full-design mean stability, historical full-design centering, donor independence, and conditional cross-unit independence give
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{evt}}\mid\mathscr F]
=\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{hist}}\mid\mathscr F]=0,
\]
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr F]
\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=CR_{\mathrm{tr}},
\]
and, by the weight bound in \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control},
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal E_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr F]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le CR_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\]
The same lemma gives
\[
\mathbb E[\mathcal B_L^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}),
\qquad
\mathbb E[\mathcal B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]\le CR_{\mathrm{don}},
\]
and \(P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_\star\).  On failure the convention in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}, bounded outcomes, and the selected-weight bound keep squared loss bounded by a fixed class constant.  Applying
\((x_1+\cdots+x_4)^2\le4\sum_jx_j^2\) therefore yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^\dagger}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le C(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee
R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}})
=CR_\star.
\]

For the converse fix a channel \(q\) and use the pair from
\texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}.  Write its target values as
\(\theta_0,\theta_1\) and \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).
Given an arbitrary estimator, test the two laws by selecting the target
closest to the estimator.  On a testing error its squared estimation
error is at least \(\Delta_q^2/4\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_0[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_0)^2]
+\mathbb E_1[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_1)^2]
&\ge\frac{\Delta_q^2}{4}
\{P_0(\phi=1)+P_1(\phi=0)\}\\
&\ge\frac{\Delta_q^2}{4}
\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}
\ge cR_q.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the maximum of the two risks is at least \(cR_q\).  Taking the
largest of the four channels gives \(cR_\star\).  All pairs lie in
\(\mathcal M^\dagger\), so the lower and upper bounds concern the same
full-design-centered causal panel class.  The covariance estimate may be
spectrally clipped because the estimator's centers use donor means and
the clipping eigenvalues stay within fixed multiples of the true
ellipticity bounds; no oracle covariance enters the fitted regression.

Finite-sample conditional coverage is
\texttt{lem:exact-full-data-interval-calibration}; taking the infimum
over \(P\in\mathcal M^\dagger\) and then the limit inferior proves the
first display.

On the good sample,
\(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\).  The deterministic
selected-weight inequality in
\texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le CB\sqrt{\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\le CB\sqrt{\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}}.
\]
Since \(\alpha\) is fixed, both are \(O(R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2})\).
Moreover that lemma gives
\[
\mathbb E[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le\left\{\mathbb E[A_L^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]\right\}^{1/2}
\le C(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee
R_{\mathrm{don}})^{1/2}.
\]
Because \(K_D,D\) are fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\),
\[
M_4(m_k)\le C,\qquad q_k\le C,\qquad
\delta_k\le CN^{-1/2},
\]
so
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}
\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{mod}}}{K_D}\sum_k(CN^{-1/2})^\kappa
\le CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\]
On the bad sample the interval length is at most \(2B\), while
\[
P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_\star
\le CR_\star^{1/2}
\]
eventually.  Combining these displays gives
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^\dagger}
\mathbb E[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}+R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}\}
\le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\]
The proof uses the full-data weight inequality, so it remains valid
when \(Th_s^d=O(1)\); no retained-block approximation or multiplier
limit is invoked.

For the lower bound, fix a channel \(q\) and choose the constants in
the corresponding construction in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}
small enough that its affinity \(a_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha\), while its
target separation remains \(\Delta_q\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}\).  If
\(\mathcal I\) has conditional coverage at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\)
under both laws, then
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_0\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in\mathcal I\mid E_0\}
&\ge P_0\{\theta_0\in\mathcal I\mid E_0\}
+P_0\{\theta_1\in\mathcal I\mid E_0\}-1\\
&\ge1-\alpha-o(1)
+\{1-\alpha-o(1)-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}-1\\
&=a_q-2\alpha-o(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
On this event the interval length is at least \(\Delta_q\).  Hence
\[
\sup_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal I)\mid E_0]
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\]
Maximizing over the four channels proves the lower bound
\(c_\alpha R_\star^{1/2}\).  The spacing pair uses affinity directly,
not a false bounded-divergence assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
Along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), the full-data selected local-polynomial construction has constants depending only on the fixed class constants such that, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\),
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\left[\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le C R_{\mathrm{tr}}
\]
on successful fits,
\[
\left\{\mathbb E_P[A_L^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]\right\}^{1/2}
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\}^{1/2},
\qquad
P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_\star,
\]
and the squared weighted generated-center displacement of the untreated surfaces is at most \(CR_{\mathrm{don}}\) in conditional expectation.  These bounds remain valid when \(Th_s^d=O(1)\); no dense-local-site or logarithmic growth condition is required.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(s,k\) and work on a successful selected fit.  The compact support of \(K\), fixed \(r,d\), and the declared selected-Gram threshold imply
\[
\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}\le Cn_sTh_{sk}^d,\qquad
\lambda_{\min}(G_{sk})\ge cn_sTh_{sk}^d,
\qquad
\sup_{w_{stk}>0}\|b_r(u_{stk})\|_2\le C.
\]
The first two inequalities are exactly the upper local-mass bound and normalized lower-eigenvalue test used by the finite dyadic selection rule.  Cauchy--Schwarz and \(G_{sk}=\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}b_r(u_{stk})b_r(u_{stk})^\top\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
&\le
\left(\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}\right)^{1/2}
\left\{\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}
\bigl(e_0^\top G_{sk}^{-1}b_r(u_{stk})\bigr)^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
&=
\left\{\left(\sum_{t,i}w_{stk}\right)
e_0^\top G_{sk}^{-1}e_0\right\}^{1/2}
\le C.
\end{aligned}
\]
The covariates and hence \(a_{stik}\) do not depend on \(i\).  Therefore
\[
\sum_t|a_{stik}|\le \frac C{n_s},\qquad
\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|
\le\frac1{K_D}\sum_k\sum_t|a_{stik}|
\le\frac C{n_s}.
\]
After squaring and summing over the \(n_s\) units,
\[
\sum_s\sum_i\left[\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le C\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=CR_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\]
This argument uses the selected Gram itself and therefore does not require \(Th_s^d\to\infty\).

We next control the selected radii.  The density lower bound, interior condition, fixed polynomial dimension, and geometric beta-mixing bound imply, for every \(v\ge0\),
\[
P\{h_{sk}>2^vh_s\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}\}
\le C\exp\{-cT(2^vh_s)^d\}
\]
until \(2^vh_s\ge1\); at the terminal grid value the failure probability is at most \(Ce^{-cT}\).  To see the displayed bound, place \(q_r\) disjoint fixed-shape subcubes inside the kernel window.  Each has conditional mass at least \(ch^d\).  Expanding the probability that a subcube is missed into successive conditional blocks and using \(\sum_{\ell\ge1}\beta_0\rho_0^\ell<\infty\) gives \(C\exp(-cTh^d)\); occupation of all subcubes makes the fixed-dimensional monomial Gram uniformly positive.  Integration of this dyadic tail yields, for every fixed \(a>0\),
\[
\mathbb E[h_{sk}^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_{sk}]
\le C\{h_s^a+T^{-a/d}\},
\qquad
P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le Ce^{-cT}.
\]
Because \(R_\star\ge R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\), the last term is at most \(CR_\star\) for all large \(T\).  Empty donor complements and \(\max_k\delta_k>\delta_0\) are absent eventually since \(K_D,D\) are fixed and \(m_k\asymp N\); all other bad events are ruled out by the finite grid and spectral clipping construction.

Polynomial reproduction follows directly from invertibility:
\[
\sum_{t,i}a_{stik}b_r(u_{stk})^\top
=e_0^\top G_{sk}^{-1}G_{sk}=e_0^\top.
\]
Taylor's formula in the maintained Holder convention therefore gives
\[
\left|
\sum_{t,i}a_{stik}m_s(X_{st})-m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})
\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t,i}|a_{stik}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda.
\]
Summing with weights \(\pi_s/K_D\) is precisely \(A_L\).  The preceding \(\ell_1\) bound and bandwidth moment bound yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E[A_L^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
&\le C\sum_s\pi_s^2
\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
+T^{-2\lambda/d}+N^{-\lambda}\right\}\\
&\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here fixed \(S\) and fixed positive \(\pi_s\) make the \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_2\) cohort aggregations equivalent up to a fixed constant, and \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\).

Finally let
\[
\Delta_k=
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\{\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_{s=1}^{S})-z_0\}\right\|_2.
\]
Euclidean projection and \(c_\Sigma I\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I\) imply
\[
\Delta_k\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}}
\left\|\frac1{m_k}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\right\|_2.
\]
Independence, centering, and \(\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\) give
\[
\mathbb E[\Delta_k^2\mid E_0]\le\frac C{m_k}.
\]
On \(\{\Delta_k\le\delta_0\}\), the upper local modulus bounds the weighted surface displacement by \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\Delta_k^\kappa\); on its complement bounded wealth and Markov's inequality apply.  Since \(0<\kappa\le1\), Jensen's inequality gives
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
\min\{B^2,C\Delta_k^{2\kappa}\}\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
\le C m_k^{-\kappa}.
\]
A fixed-fold average and Cauchy--Schwarz now give \(CR_{\mathrm{don}}\).  This proves every assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), the full-data interval in \texttt{def:honest-interval} obeys
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
whenever its deterministic class constants and donor fold sizes are defined.  The statement is finite-sample; it uses separate bounded-summand calibration for the historical and event components and the fourth-moment donor calibration, joined only by Bonferroni.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr F=\sigma(\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\), where \(\mathscr X\) is the complete historical design.  Since \(z_0=\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]\), adjoining \(z_0\) does not enlarge \(\sigma(E_0)\).  Donor independence and the two full-design restrictions give
\[
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr F]=0,\qquad
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr F]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0].
\]
Conditional cross-unit independence makes the unit-level pairs consisting of a complete historical error path and an event observation independent across \((s,i)\), conditional on \(\mathscr F\).

On a good sample, polynomial reproduction and Taylor's formula, as proved in \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control}, give
\[
\left|
\sum_{s,t,i}\pi_s\bar a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})
-\frac1{K_D}\sum_{s,k}\pi_sm_s(\widetilde z_{sk})
\right|\le A_L.
\]
The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the full-data estimator identity therefore yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
={}&
\sum_{s,i}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\right\}\\
&-\sum_{s,i}\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}
-\mathcal B_L-\mathcal B_{\mathrm{don}},
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(|\mathcal B_L|\le A_L\) and
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{don}}
=\frac1{K_D}\sum_k\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_{sk})-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]

For completeness, the bounded-sum inequality used twice follows from convexity.  If \(W\in[a,b]\) and \(\mathbb E[W]=0\), then
\[
\mathbb E[e^{tW}]
\le\exp\{t^2(b-a)^2/8\}.
\]
Multiplying this bound for conditionally independent summands and applying Markov's inequality to both signs gives
\[
P\left\{\left|\sum_\nu W_\nu\right|>x\,\middle|\,\mathscr F\right\}
\le2\exp\left\{-\frac{2x^2}{\sum_\nu(b_\nu-a_\nu)^2}\right\}.
\]
For a historical unit, the centered contribution
\[
W_{si}^{\mathrm{hist}}
=\pi_s\sum_t\bar a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}
\]
has conditional range length at most
\[
B\pi_s\sum_t|\bar a_{sti}|,
\]
because \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\) and its conditional mean is subtracted.  Consequently
\[
P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s,i}W_{si}^{\mathrm{hist}}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr F\right\}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\]
Likewise each centered event summand has range length \(B\pi_s/n_s\), so
\[
P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s,i}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}\right|
>R_{\mathrm{evt}}\,\middle|\,\mathscr F\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\]
These are separate probability bounds.  No independence between the event and historical variable of the same unit has been used.

For the donor term, independence and standardization give
\[
\mathbb E[Y_j\mid E_0]=0,\qquad
\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\]
Expanding the fourth power of the norm of the standardized complementary-fold sum and retaining the index patterns in which every index occurs at least twice gives
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
\left\|m_k^{-1/2}\sum_{j\notin k}Y_j\right\|_2^4
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
\le
\frac{B}{m_k}
+\left(1-\frac1{m_k}\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(m_k).
\]
Markov's inequality, the projection and ellipticity conversion, and the definition of \(q_k,\delta_k\) imply
\[
P\!\left\{
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}
\{\operatorname{vec}((\widetilde z_{sk})_s)-z_0\}\right\|_2
>\delta_k\,\middle|\,E_0\right\}
\le\frac{\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}}{K_D}.
\]

Fix
\[

\]
Use the full donor folds, projected complementary-fold centers, bandwidth grid, selection rule, and raw full-data local-polynomial fits of \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  On every successful fit define
\[

a_{stik}=e_0^\top G_{sk}^{-1}w_{stk}b_r(u_{stk}),
\qquad

\]
Then
\[
\widehat m_s=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\bar a_{sti}Q_{sti},
\qquad

\left(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s\right).
\]
Put
\[

\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
|a_{stik}|\,\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{sk}\|_2^\lambda,
\]

For donor fold \(k\), retain the full-covariance calibration
\[
D=Sd,\qquad
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),\qquad
M_4(m_k)=\frac{B}{m_k}

\[

proposed.statement:
Let \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) be the subclass in \texttt{def:full-design-centered-class}.  There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class constants, such that along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), uniformly for \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) and \(P\)-almost every \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\),

\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_\star.
\]
The raw feasible estimator in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator} attains the upper bound with nonidentically distributed bounded event outcomes, an unknown heteroskedastic donor law, and estimated full \(\Sigma\).

prose_updates.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. A maintained event-transport restriction identifies it from the full historical wealth-path regression, and the raw generated-center local-polynomial estimator is exactly a foldwise weighted-panel event coefficient. The original panel-law class is too broad: a shared design-measurable component can defeat replication and any vanishing honest expected length. On the transparent subclass \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), which adds the two explicit strong full-design mean-stability and error-centering restrictions, the sharp risk is \(R_\star\) and the sharp honest expected-length rate is \(R_\star^{1/2}\). A full-data interval combines exact bounded-summand historical and event radii, observable Holder bias, and a full-covariance fourth-moment donor allowance. The positive-probability joint causal-panel embedding supplies matching treated, smoothing, spacing, and donor lower bounds; only affinity, not bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence, is claimed for spacing.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal financial event-study, repeated-measurement regression, generated-regressor, and synthetic-control interval results do not jointly cover a realized external donor center, shared calendar design, finite-cohort causal identification, and an all-relative-growth minimax and honest-length frontier. The unrepaired panel class also shows why conditional cross-unit independence alone is insufficient for replication rates.
project_justification.niche: The design observes historical proxy coordinates exactly, replicates untreated wealth responses at shared calendar sites, and estimates only the event query from an independent donor universe. The analysis makes the required full-design strict-exogeneity and centering restrictions explicit instead of attributing them to weaker contemporaneous or cross-unit conditions.
project_justification.fill: The project proves event-transport identification, an exact raw-estimator FWL representation, positive-probability joint causal-panel lower-bound embeddings, and sharp risk and honest expected-length frontiers on \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\). The attaining interval uses the full-data estimator with exact bounded-summand radii, Taylor bias, and full-covariance donor calibration, including sparse spacing regimes without a block-multiplier approximation.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with density bounded above and away from zero; the calendar process is geometrically beta mixing. The sharp upper and interval results additionally impose full-design centering of every historical regression error.
sampling_model.units: At every shared pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) bounded response replicates, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) bounded treated wealth levels. Unit histories and event outcomes are independent across units conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), while event and history variables for the same unit may remain dependent.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cohort-average event-transport equality identify the causal target. For the sharp rates, event conditional means must also be stable given the complete historical design; this strong restriction is not implied by cross-unit independence.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path belongs to an interior positive-probability region, historical design densities are bounded below there, and donor displacements used by the modulus remain inside the declared local radius.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent donor sample estimates only the event query under an unknown full heteroskedastic covariance; historical coordinates are exact. Donor-fold projected means and selected full-data local-polynomial fits form \(\widehat\tau\). Inference uses exact conditional bounded-summand radii for historical and event components, an observable Taylor allowance, and a fourth-moment full-covariance donor radius, with Bonferroni calibration.

prose_updates.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu motivate causal financial panels and the volatility sensitivity of compounded wealth; causal identification here still rests on the maintained event-transport equality. Yan, Yao, and Zhou and Gaiffas inform repeated-response and pointwise random-design smoothing, while Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle and Delaigle, Hall, and Meister clarify why an estimated external query differs from generated training coordinates or classical measurement error. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik motivate separating stochastic and approximation uncertainty, but the final interval does not invoke retained-block multipliers. Chen and Christensen inform weak-dependence Gram control. Armstrong and Kolesar motivate honest expected-length comparisons, while the present lower bound is embedded in positive-probability causal panel laws. The field-tier additions are the exact FWL identity, joint-law embedding, higher-smoothness donor saturation, and all-relative-regime frontier on the explicitly full-design-centered subclass.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality. The donor converse remains conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus, which excludes flat surfaces and is not derived for the whole Holder ball. Sharp risk and honest expected length are proved only over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), whose event full-design mean stability and historical full-design error centering are explicit strong restrictions and are not consequences of conditional cross-unit independence or contemporaneous regression. The obstruction proposition shows that the original class cannot support either advertised vanishing rate. Mean-only return-path nonidentification concerns only \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\), not equivalence of the full historical wealth panels.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution comprises the positive-probability joint causal-panel embedding, event-transport identifying map, exact raw-estimator FWL representation, higher-smoothness donor saturation, and sharp all-relative-growth risk and honest expected-length frontiers on \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\). The original panel-law class remains subject to the shared-design replication obstruction; no alternative interval is claimed to repair its \(R_\star^{1/2}\) rate. The donor lower bound assumes the two-sided local modulus. The result does not claim event-date exchangeability, identification from mean-only return matching, smoothness adaptation, sharp phase-intersection constants, growing cohort count, or growing proxy-path dimension.
